scope: Independent visual comparison against the exact factual H45 source. Text, metrics, self-declared PASS labels and the producer's own embedded reference are non-authoritative.
observations: The exact source visibly contains two separate telescopic-slide pieces arranged diagonally.
The generated candidate depicts a materially different dominant assembled-rail topology rather than preserving the two factual source pieces.
Visible hole/slot patterns and terminal structures do not correspond closely enough to the exact source to pass the factual-identity gate.
The generated object is visually plausible as furniture hardware, which explains the strong normal-view visual impression, but plausibility is not source fidelity.
researchConsequence: Normal-size human plausibility review is insufficient for factual product-image generation.
Independent comparison must use the exact source bytes, not a source depiction regenerated inside the producer output.
Piece topology and landmark patterns must be gated before presentation quality can matter.
A visually excellent failure remains useful evidence about capability but cannot be promoted as a faithful product variant.
